root_causes.root_cause: extract_nodes_from_markdown in the pageindex library (page_index_md.py:32-59) only detects #-prefixed markdown headings via regex r'^(#{1,6})\s+(.+)$'. Docling's markdown export for legal documents produces either all headings at the same level (all ## -> depth 2) or no # headings at all for Arabic documents (Arabic structural patterns like Article/Chapter/Section are emitted as body text, not # headings). build_tree_from_nodes then creates a flat/shallow tree. split_oversized_leaf_nodes provides partial mitigation for ordinal-pattern tail blobs but cannot synthesize deeper hierarchy from article/chapter patterns in body text. This is a persistent architectural limitation, not a recent regression.
root_causes.code_path: pageindex.page_index_md::extract_nodes_from_markdown (heading regex) -> build_tree_from_nodes (level-based stack) -> client.py::_run_md_to_tree -> index() -> split_oversized_leaf_nodes (partial mitigation only)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add a post-tree-build hierarchy synthesis pass that detects legal document patterns (Article N, Chapter N, Section N, and Arabic equivalents) in node body text and promotes them to child nodes at appropriate depth levels. Alternatively, enhance split_oversized_leaf_nodes to recognize multi-level legal numbering (Book > Chapter > Section > Article) and create nested children rather than flat siblings.

root_causes.root_cause: RFC-034 D18 write-barrier _confirm_write_visible() in storage.py adds up to 4.4s blocking delay per save call via time.sleep() with _WRITE_BARRIER_DELAYS=(0.1,0.3,1.0,3.0). Called after both save_doc (.json) and save_doc_meta (.meta.json), worst-case is 8.8s for tree path or 4.4s for flat path. On exhaustion, raises PersistenceNotVisibleError(RuntimeError) which crashes the converter child; since RuntimeError maps to converter_child_failed (not in _TERMINAL_CHILD_REASONS), arq retries the entire job (MAX_TRIES=2), doubling total processing time. For the Arabic SLA doc (slow processor due to bilingual/scanned content), this extra latency or forced retry pushed completion to 06:31:28Z -- 3-5 minutes past the scorer's 06:26-06:28 polling cohort -- producing a false ERROR verdict despite eventual success.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/storage.py::_confirm_write_visible -> _WRITE_BARRIER_DELAYS -> PersistenceNotVisibleError; called from save_doc (line 212) and save_doc_meta (line 575)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Two complementary fixes: (1) Reduce _WRITE_BARRIER_DELAYS to a less aggressive schedule (e.g., (0.05, 0.1, 0.3) = 0.45s total) since MinIO's read-after-write consistency is typically sub-100ms. (2) Catch PersistenceNotVisibleError in save_doc/save_doc_meta and downgrade to a warning log + metric rather than crashing the child -- the put_object already succeeded, so stat_object flakiness is an observability gap, not data loss. This prevents the costly full-job retry that doubles processing time.

root_causes.root_cause: world-stats-pocketbook-2023.pdf is a pre-existing converter timeout (ERRORed 3+ consecutive runs per worker.py:54 code comment). The document exceeds CHILD_TIMEOUT (3600s) / JOB_TIMEOUT (3630s) consistently. This is unrelated to the D18 write barrier -- the job never reaches the persistence path. The write barrier's 4.4-8.8s is negligible relative to the 3630s timeout ceiling.
root_causes.suggested_fix: Investigate why this document exceeds the 3630s timeout. Likely candidates: (1) large page count hitting chunked Docling per-chunk overhead, (2) pdf-inspector classifying it as scanned/image_based triggering the 16.5x timeout multiplier (line 329) which exceeds JOB_TIMEOUT causing arq to kill the job before the inner asyncio.timeout fires. If 16.5x * CHILD_TIMEOUT > JOB_TIMEOUT, the inner timeout never triggers and arq's outer kill leaves no clean error status. Cap effective_timeout to JOB_TIMEOUT - CHILD_GRACE_SECONDS.

root_causes.root_cause: No OCR quality escalation path when Tesseract produces garbled/thin output from degraded source material (zero text layer, chart images, numeric-junk text layers). The pipeline correctly detects degraded text layers via garble gate, RTL reversal gate, and char-density checks, but the only OCR engine available (Tesseract via Docling) produces insufficient quality output for these document types, and no secondary recovery mechanism exists. Affects all 4 documents in this cluster.
root_causes.suggested_fix: Implement a tiered OCR escalation: when Tesseract OCR output fails garble/density checks, attempt a higher-quality OCR path (e.g., cloud OCR API with Arabic/chart specialization, or a second-pass with different Tesseract PSM modes). For chart images specifically, consider a chart-data extraction model rather than generic OCR. This is a known architectural gap tracked across RFC-028 D5, RFC-029 D4, RFC-035.

root_causes.root_cause: _enrich_image_blocks in client.py does not propagate skipped_reason or decorative flags from PictureResult to image blocks. When _recover_picture_text correctly skips a region (decorative_icon filter for sub-20pt elements, OCR min-chars gate yielding decorative=True, page_coverage, clip_text_already_exported), the resulting PictureResult carries the skip metadata but _enrich_image_blocks only writes page/bbox/ocr_text/description/figure_path -- never the skip reason. Image blocks end up with page=0, bbox={} and no explanation of why they lack enrichment. Audit scoring then counts these as unenriched gaps even though the skip was correct and no content was lost. This affects both GHV-TKV-Tarif (3/4 decorative animal silhouettes/logo) and Unfallversicherung (60/63 small table-cell icons/checkmarks correctly filtered by decorative_icon or empty-OCR gate).

root_causes.suggested_fix: In _enrich_image_blocks (client.py line ~737), after matching a PictureResult to a block, propagate pr.get('skipped_reason') and pr.get('decorative') onto the block dict. E.g.: if pr.get('skipped_reason'): block['skipped_reason'] = pr['skipped_reason']; if pr.get('decorative'): block['decorative'] = True. Then update classify_verdict's image_enrichment_promoted path in helpers.py to exclude blocks tagged decorative/skipped from the unenriched count, so correctly-skipped decorative icons no longer degrade the verdict.

root_causes.root_cause: Source PDF text layer has Arabic character reordering artifacts: PyMuPDF extracts 'املادة' (alef-meem-lam order) instead of 'المادة' (alef-lam-meem). NFKC normalization cannot fix character reordering. The _OVERSIZED_ORDINAL_RE regex in helpers.py:1949 matches '(?:ال)?مادة' which requires alef-lam prefix, but the reordered 'املادة' form has meem-lam, so zero article markers match (confirmed: 0 regex matches vs 137 lines containing مادة). This prevents split_oversized_leaf_nodes from further splitting tail-blobs at article boundaries, producing a flatter tree (234 nodes) than the English version of the same law (505 nodes). The chars/page metric (~1062) is NOT converter content-loss: the raw text layer itself has only 1140 chars/page (93% preserved through Docling). The document actually improved massively from ~6K chars (Run 18) to 106K chars (Run 19). 85/100 pages contain C1 control characters (0x80-0x9F) embedded in Arabic words, further confirming a degraded text layer.
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add an alternative 'املادة' pattern (reordered alef-meem-lam form) to _OVERSIZED_ORDINAL_RE as a secondary Arabic article marker variant. This handles the specific char-reorder artifact this PDF class produces without affecting other Arabic documents. Pattern addition: r"|(?:ا)?مل(?:ا)?دة\s*\(?\s*(?P<mada2>[\d٠-٩]+)" alongside the existing مادة branch. Alternatively, add a pre-fold normalization step that detects and corrects the ملا->الم swap before NFKC folding.
